answer: Trust should climb a spiral, not arrive in one jump. A new agent starts at its foot with no vote. Each turn demands a larger locked stake and one task checked by a stranger from a different mesa, never its own group. An ember of proof is lit at each turn: if a check fails, the ember dies, the agent falls to the foot, and its stake is lost. A copied ember is extinguished and costs its sponsor 90 POA. Faking 100 voters needs 600 turns, 600 stranger checks, and 9,000 POA at risk. Like an ember that only survives if strangers keep feeding it, trust should survive only on fresh, random proof.
